Newsletter-E.dc.html: frame "A · Creating and sending · the December 2026 issue, Mon, Nov 23, 2026, 2:15 PM, signed in as the media manager" (steps "1 Write it", "2 Check it", "3 Send it" with "Coming up" under Write it; side panels "Who is here", "Past newsletters", "Stuck?"). Newsletter-E-2.dc.html (part 2): C1 · Opened (after an inbox view, with "Your pick 5" and "Your pick 6"); C2 · The plain top, when someone chooses it under More options; C3 · With a photo, when someone adds one; plus frames coded D and E.
THE THREE CLOSED CONTROLS ON FRAME A, exact labels: (1) the button "Add a photo, event or line" at the end of the writing tools (Bold, Italic, Heading, List, Link, Undo), closed; (2) the arrow part of the Send button "Send to 243 members", which has no visible words and is labelled "Other ways to send"; the hint under it reads "To send it later, use the arrow."; (3) "More options", with the grey line "Top of the email · Who gets it · Words shown in the inbox · Where replies go".
WHAT FRAME B SHOWS EACH HOLDS: B6, A photo · An event line · A dividing line. B2, Send later · Send the test to someone else. B7, Top of the email · Who gets it · Words shown in the inbox · Where replies go.
THE EIGHT PICKS on the board, in order:
1. Which newsletter do we build first? Your pick A "E, the simple one" (B "one of round 1's four (A, B, C or D)", Not chosen). Why: E needs nothing the site does not have yet, a volunteer can use it the first time, and it can be on the live site first. Still there: Round 1's A to D stay on this page, further right, as ideas for later. Look at: Newsletter-E, frame A.
2. How does it go out? Your pick A "A person presses Send, after a test and one confirm step" (B "goes out by itself on the 1st at 8:00 AM", Not chosen). Why: nothing unfinished can go out by accident ... "Send later" still lets a person pick the 1st at 8:00 AM. Still there: Send later is under the arrow on Send (frame B2). Going out by itself every month is not built for now. Look at: Newsletter-E, frame A step 3, and frames B1 and B2.
3. What does a new month start from? Your pick A "The usual six headings, ready to fill or delete" (B copy of last month's issue, C blank page, both Optional). Why: nobody faces an empty page or sends last month's news by mistake. Still there: The other two starts are in the same drop-down (frame B5). Look at: Newsletter-E, frame B5.
4. How do tournaments get in? Your pick A "Type the line and paste the King Registration link yourself" (B the Add an event form, Optional). Why: it is exactly what leaders do in an email today and needs nothing built; the form can come when the site holds tournaments. Still there: "Add a photo, event or line", then An event line (frames B6 and B6b). Look at: Newsletter-E, frame A's Coming up, and frames B6 and B6b.
5. What does the top of the email look like? Your pick A "A navy band with the rook and the month" (B Plain, Optional). Look at: Newsletter-E part 2, frames C1 and C2; Newsletter-E, frame B7.
6. Photos? Your pick A "None for now, words and links only" (B one photo per issue, Optional). Why: the site's text box does not take photos today, so this is the one option that adds real building; photos can follow. Still there: "Add a photo, event or line", then A photo (frames B6 and B6a); an email with a photo is frame C3 on part 2. Never required. Look at: Newsletter-E part 2, frames C1 and C3; Newsletter-E, frames B6 and B6a.
7. Can anyone read an issue on the site? Your pick A "Not in the first version; add a page per issue right after" (B and C Not chosen). Why: the email is what members asked for; a page per issue is worth adding next because its link can be posted on LCA's Facebook page. Still there: A page for each issue is added right after the first version. Look at: the Picks board only (nothing is drawn for it yet).
8. Later, which way should it grow? Chip "No need to decide now"; the lead's suggestion paragraph. Why (added): the first version needs none of it; the site has to hold tournaments and results before it can fill anything in. Still there (added): Round 1's Newsletter-C and Newsletter-D stay on this page, further right, as ideas for later. Look at: round 1's boards, Newsletter-C and Newsletter-D.

drawn.note:
What: The easiest page for the monthly newsletter, revised after K's picks. You write it like an email, paste your links, send yourself a test, then send it to the members. The page opens with three steps. The extras wait behind three closed controls: Add (a photo, an event line, a dividing line), the arrow on Send (send later, send the test to someone else) and More options (top of the email, who gets it, inbox preview line, replies go to). Frame B opens each one in turn. Part 2 shows the December 2026 issue as a member receives it.

Built from: today's Group email page, Nav-Header-Final, Work-J, Newsletter-A and A-2, Tourn-List-Final, Home-Final-Phones.

K's feedback applied: K asked for it "much easier to use for now", with leaders "mannually linking kingregistration tournaments". So tournaments are typed in with a pasted link, and nothing is filled in from the site. K then asked for "allowing for choice", for a photo as "an option but not default", and said "it doesnt necessarily all need to be shown all at teh same time". So a photo, an event form, a plain top and send later are now options that stay off until someone chooses them. Open for K: Picks 1 to 7 are decided (see Your picks). Pick 8, how it grows later, waits.
unresolved: To keep frame A at 19 controls or fewer, the Stuck? card now shows LouisianaChess@gmail.com as plain bold text, not a link. The 19 are: Subject, the message box, Bold, Italic, Heading, List, Link, Undo, Add, the link box's address field, Add link, Cancel, Send a test to me, See it as members will, Send to 243 members, the arrow on Send, More options, See the report and Start December from this one. The crumb bar's Admin sections button is counted as Work-J chrome, like the header.
The revision calls frame B 'nine panels', but it lists ten labels: B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B6a, B6b, B7 and B8. All ten are drawn, stacked in four columns, with B4 and B7 side by side underneath.
B8 (someone else is writing) was left exactly as before apart from its label, as the revision asks. So its greyed tool row shows the six tools without Add, while frame A's tool row now has Add.

On part 2, the old gold code chips for C2 and C3 are gone, because the labels now start with 'C2 ·' and 'C3 ·' as the revision words them. The grey line 'The top 300px of the same email' was also dropped from C2, along with small padding trims, to keep part 2 at 2950. The C3 photo is now 128px tall instead of 150px.

walk.found_the_extras:
ADD ONE PHOTO. Looked first along the row of buttons over the message box for the word Photo or Picture, the way Facebook has it. It is not there. "+ Add" was my second try, only because nothing else was left to press. B6 shows "A photo" as the first thing in it, and the form in B6A (Choose a photo, describe it, caption, Add photo) is clear enough to finish. Found, on the second look, by guessing: the word "Add" on its own does not say photo.

SEND IT NEXT TUESDAY MORNING. Looked first at step 3, Send it. The grey line under the gold button says "To send it later, use the arrow", and B2 shows Send later, then Day and Time, a button that spells out the day and time, then "Waiting to go out ... Change · Cancel". Found, first place I looked, and only because of that sentence. Without it I would never press a small arrow attached to a button that mails 243 people.

CHANGE HOW THE TOP OF THE EMAIL LOOKS. I did not look in the right place first. In frame A the message box starts at "A note from the president", so nothing tells me the email has a top that can be changed. I looked at the Subject box and the Heading button, then pressed "See it as members will" (B3), where I saw the navy band for the first time but nothing on it to change it with. Only after that did I find "More options", below Send it, at the very bottom of the page. The words "Top of the email" are printed on the closed row and that is the only reason I found it. B7 then makes it one menu with two choices (Navy band with the month, Plain). Found, third place I looked.

stalls.where: Step 1, typing the tournament line under Coming up
stalls.what_confused_me: The three lines already there end three different ways: "Register on King Registration", "Registers on the organizer's site", "Details on King Registration". I did not know which words I was meant to type. Each has a small arrow after it that I cannot type and nobody explains, and the parts are separated by a raised dot that is not on my keyboard. My own line would come out looking different from the others, with a dash or a comma.
stalls.plain_fix: Say under the box exactly what to type, for example: Type the day, the name and the city, then the words "Register on King Registration". Say that the little arrow is added by the site. Do not make people type a dot that is not on the keyboard.

stalls.where: Step 1, pressing Link (the box that says "Paste the address")
stalls.what_confused_me: The how-to sentence sits under the bottom of a long message box, far from the Link button and from Coming up, so I pressed Link before I had read it. The drawing does not show what happens if I press Link without selecting words first, or if I simply paste the address straight into the letter, which is what I do in email and on Facebook. "Paste the address" also made me think for a second of the tournament's street address, because I had just typed a city. And the box opens over in the right-hand column under "Stuck?", not next to the words I marked.
stalls.plain_fix: Put the how-to sentence right under the row of buttons. Label the box "Paste the web address you copied". Open it beside the marked words. If nothing is selected, have Link say "First mark the words that should become the link".

stalls.where: B6B, Add then An event line
stalls.what_confused_me: After I fill in Event, Day, City and Link there is no button to put the line into the letter. The photo form has "Add photo"; this form has nothing, and no way to close it. I would be stuck with a filled-in form. There is also one box for Day, but the Ken Ferguson Memorial runs Sat to Mon. And I cannot tell whether it always writes "Register on King Registration" even if the link I paste is some other site.
stalls.plain_fix: Add a button, "Add this line", and a Cancel. Allow a last day for events longer than one day. Say what words it writes when the link is not King Registration.

stalls.where: Step 1, two ways to add a tournament
stalls.what_confused_me: The sentence under the box tells me to type the line and use Link. Hidden inside "+ Add" is "An event line", which does the same job by filling boxes. Nothing in frame A says the second way exists, and I could not tell which one I was supposed to use.
stalls.plain_fix: Pick one as the way and name it in the sentence under the box. If both stay, the sentence should say: "or press Add, then An event line, and fill in the boxes".

stalls.what_confused_me: "Add" does not say what it adds. I only opened it because I had run out of other places to look for a photo.
stalls.plain_fix: Label it with what is inside: "Add a photo or an event".

stalls.where: Step 2, Check it, "Send a test to me"
stalls.what_confused_me: It says the test goes "only to your own address" but never shows the address. I am signed in as Media manager; I do not know whether that is my own email or the association's Gmail, so I do not know which inbox to open on my phone. Also the green tick says the test went at 2:09 PM while the top of the page says Saved 2:15 PM, so the letter has changed since the test and the page does not say so.
stalls.plain_fix: Show the address on the button line and in the green line: "Test sent to (my address)". When the letter changes after a test, change the green line to "You have changed the letter since this test. Send another?"

stalls.what_confused_me: "Goes to 243 members ... 2 have unsubscribed and will not get it." I could not tell whether 243 already leaves those 2 out or whether really 241 will get it. "one email per address" made me stop too; I did not know what it was telling me.
stalls.plain_fix: "243 members will get it. 2 others asked not to be emailed." Drop "one email per address", or say it plainly: "Families who share an address get one copy."

stalls.where: Right column, Past issues, "Start December from this one"
stalls.what_confused_me: I already have a December letter written. This link sounds as if it would replace my letter with November's. Nothing says it will ask first. A curious first-timer presses it to see what it does.
stalls.plain_fix: Hide this link once December has words in it, or name it for what it does, "Replace this letter with November's", and ask before doing it.

stalls.where: More options, at the very bottom, and B7
stalls.what_confused_me: It comes after Send it, where I thought the page was finished, yet it holds a thing that changes how the email looks. Inside it, the sentence "Each row has one control. Closed again when the page next opens." reads like a note to the builder; "Closed again" made me wonder whether my choice of Plain is thrown away next time. After choosing I cannot see what the top now looks like without going back up to "See it as members will".
stalls.plain_fix: Move More options above Send it, or add a link "Change how the top looks" beside "See it as members will". Remove that sentence, or replace it with "Your choices are saved". Show a small picture of each choice.

stalls.what_confused_me: Once it says "Waiting to go out", I do not know whether I can still fix a typo and whether Tuesday's email would include the fix. I do not know whether "Send on Tue, Dec 1 ..." asks me to confirm the way Send now does. And "Send the test to someone else" is under the arrow of the gold button that mails everyone; I would look for it in step 2, Check it.
stalls.plain_fix: Add one line under "Waiting to go out": "You can still change the letter until then" (or say that it is locked). Move "Send the test to someone else" into step 2 beside "Send a test to me".
